name: proposals-ontology
what: Larkspur's tour, Wed Feb 7 (the normal day): the Ontology page with backup_jobs open; under it, Proposed from the data (ADR 0022 §5, Q-139, Q-213): the controller column's four values, a band for the last job's common value and the recovery point's three values, each saying what it rests on and what accepting it does, with Accept… and Not now for the owner

pageText: Each is listed as one of its codes, meaning itself until someone words it.
Bands for the common value of Last job
Each band is its usual range five points either side. A day outside one holds the day, by the values check.

name: proposals-quality
what: The same day, tls's Quality tab: under its checks, Proposed from the data: the ingress, issuer and protocol columns' values and a band for private_link, nothing applying until accepted

text: Bands for the 2 common values of private_link

name: proposals-accept-form
what: On the Ontology page (backup_jobs left open), the owner taps Accept… on the controller's values: a reason, the day it takes effect from (the next day to arrive, Mon Apr 1, by default) and what it reaches, and Accept, which waits for the reason

pageText: No recorded day moves: each keeps the rules it ran under.

name: proposals-accepted
what: The reason typed and Accept tapped: the values are a change set in force from Mon Apr 1, recorded at once; the card says so with the reason, and the flow's changes list it
clicks: Every backup job is run by one of the four controllers.

expect.status: ^Accepted from the data: List the 4 values of controller, in force from Mon Apr 1\. Recorded\.
pageText: Accepted, in force from Mon Apr 1: “Every backup job is run by one of the four controllers.”
